common_name: Graffiti Red Lace Pentas (Red Flowers with White Lace-Patterned Eye)

planting.note: Set out transplants once soil has warmed after the last frost in well-drained, fertile beds or containers in full sun; the white, lace-like veining over the red petals shows most clearly in strong light and consistent summer heat.

directions: Graffiti Red Lace is a bicolor selection within the compact Graffiti seed series, its red florets overlaid with a feathery white pattern that gives each flower cluster a frosted, lace-like look. Plants form a tight, well-branched mound that stays in bloom from late spring through frost without routine deadheading. Like other pentas, the dense clusters of tubular flowers are a dependable nectar source for butterflies and a favorite stop for hummingbirds throughout the Gulf Coast growing season. Use it in mixed containers or massed in beds, where its patterned color reads differently from solid-red pentas nearby.

common_name: Butterfly Deep Rose Pentas (Heat-Proof Rose-Red Star-Cluster Hummingbird Plant)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Butterfly Deep Rose carries a more vivid, saturated rose-red tone than the related 'Butterfly Deep Pink' already grown in the Butterfly series.

directions: Butterfly Deep Rose is a vigorous, large-flowered color in the PanAmerican Seed Butterfly series, grown from vegetative cuttings for uniform, early branching plants. Its wide umbels of rose-red florets bloom continuously from spring planting through the first fall frost, holding color well through Gulf Coast heat and humidity. The flower clusters are sized and shaped for easy hummingbird feeding and draw steady butterfly traffic all season, making this a dependable pollinator anchor for beds, borders, and large containers. Site it in full sun with consistent moisture for the heaviest bloom.

common_name: Butterfly Orchid Pentas (Heat-Proof Coral-Pink Star-Cluster Pollinator Plant)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Butterfly Orchid's soft coral-pink color is a distinct shade from the rose, red, and lavender tones already grown in the Butterfly series.

directions: Butterfly Orchid is a coral-pink color in the mid-size PanAmerican Seed Butterfly series, bred for large flower umbels on well-branched, uniform plants. It tolerates summer rain and heavy heat without losing bloom quality, flowering steadily from late spring into mid fall. The broad, flat flower clusters give butterflies an easy landing surface and supply nectar through the hottest stretch of the growing season when many other bedding plants stall out. Pair it with cooler-toned Butterfly series colors for a layered pollinator border.

common_name: New Look Red Pentas (Compact Early-Blooming Seed Pentas Series)

planting.note: Set out transplants after soil has warmed following the last frost, spacing plants close together to form a dense, uniform mound; New Look is an older, compact seed series bred for early, heavy bloom.

directions: New Look Red is the scarlet-red color in one of the longest-established dwarf seed pentas series, valued for staying noticeably shorter and more compact than taller pentas types while still flowering heavily. It branches early and densely from a young transplant, filling in beds and container edges quickly with clusters of star-shaped blooms. The abundant, continuously produced flower heads keep butterflies and hummingbirds working the bed all summer, even in a planting too small for taller pentas selections. Its tidy habit makes it well suited to front-of-border and mass bedding use.

common_name: New Look Pink Pentas (Compact Early-Blooming Seed Pentas Series)

planting.note: Set out transplants after soil has warmed following the last frost, spacing plants close together to form a dense, uniform mound; New Look is an older, compact seed series bred for early, heavy bloom.

directions: New Look Pink produces creamy light-pink flower clusters on the same small, densely branched plants that define the New Look seed series, one of the earliest compact pentas lines widely sold through garden centers. Its early and continuous flowering habit gives pollinators a nectar source almost as soon as transplants establish, well ahead of many taller pentas types. The soft pink color mixes easily with both pastel and bold-colored bedding companions. Deadheading is not required, since spent clusters are quickly hidden by new growth.

common_name: New Look White Pentas (Compact Early-Blooming Seed Pentas Series)

planting.note: Set out transplants after soil has warmed following the last frost, spacing plants close together to form a dense, uniform mound; New Look is an older, compact seed series bred for early, heavy bloom.

directions: New Look White carries pure white flower clusters on the same compact, tidy plants shared across the New Look seed series, making it a reliable brightener for evening and night gardens. Flowering starts early from a young transplant and continues without interruption through the growing season. Butterflies and hummingbirds visit the clustered white blooms as readily as any other pentas color, and the pale flowers show especially well planted against darker-leaved or darker-flowered neighbors. Its small stature suits window boxes and tight bed edges where taller pentas would overwhelm the space.

common_name: New Look Violet Pentas (Compact Early-Blooming Seed Pentas Series)

planting.note: Set out transplants after soil has warmed following the last frost, spacing plants close together to form a dense, uniform mound; New Look is an older, compact seed series bred for early, heavy bloom.

directions: New Look Violet rounds out the New Look seed series with rich violet-purple flower clusters on the same small, uniform, well-branched plants. It completes an early-blooming color range alongside New Look Red, Pink, and White, giving gardeners a full compact pentas palette from a single seed line. The violet tone reads as a cooler, deeper companion to the warmer colors in the series and attracts the same steady traffic of butterflies and bees typical of pentas. Its dwarf habit keeps it in scale with other small bedding annuals in mixed plantings.
